holidays.name: National Mole Day
holidays.description: Chemistry fans celebrate the mole, the science unit for counting atoms and molecules, with puns, parties, and cute mole-themed crafts. Some cheerful celebrants even bake mole-shaped treats, and others just wear their lab coats with pride.
holidays.origin: Mole Day is celebrated from 6:02 a.m. to 6:02 p.m. on 10/23 as a nod to Avogadro's number, 6.02 × 10^23. It grew out of chemistry teaching circles and is now an annual tradition in classrooms.
holidays.funFact: One mole of anything contains about 602 sextillion particles. That is enough rubber ducks to cover the Earth many times over.

holidays.name: National Boston Cream Pie Day
holidays.description: A day for sinking your fork into a layered sponge cake filled with vanilla custard and topped with glossy chocolate. It is a classic dessert with a misleading name, and it is delicious anyway.
holidays.origin: The dessert dates to 19th-century Boston, where cakes were commonly baked in pie tins. That is how a cake ended up being called a pie. National Boston Cream Pie Day is an unofficial food observance.
holidays.funFact: Boston cream pie is the official dessert of Massachusetts. It was chosen in 1996 after a student campaign.

holidays.name: National TV Talk Show Host Day
holidays.description: A salute to the hosts who keep us company with monologues, celebrity chats, and couch-side banter. Pick a favorite late-night legend and watch some classic clips.
holidays.origin: The day is tied to the birthday of Johnny Carson, who was born on October 23, 1925. He hosted The Tonight Show for three decades.
holidays.funFact: Johnny Carson hosted The Tonight Show from 1962 to 1992, a span of 30 years.
